For applicants from the fields of human medicine, veterinary medicine and dentistry, further subject-specific regulations apply

documents: Full curriculum vitae in tabular form (max. 3 pages) and a list of published publications (max. 10 pages; mandatory for postdocs)
Letter of motivation (1-2 pages) and a proposal of the research project (max. 10 pages) agreed with the academic adviser in Germany, plus a time schedule of the planned research work
Proof of admission to doctoral studies / enrolment in doctoral studies (for doctoral students)
Confirmation from the academic host in Germany referring to the project and guaranteeing a workplace, and the declaration from the scientific supervisor on safety-relevant and ethical aspects
All university degree certificates already obtained, stating final grades (a provisional document if the most recent is not yet available), plus Transcripts of Records with individual grades
One recent supporting letter of recommendation on a DAAD form from a university teacher (for doctoral students, from the doctoral thesis supervisor)
selection_criteria: Academic qualification: grade point average, development of grades, academic progress, knowledge of the language(s) of instruction or working language(s), and scholarly achievements after graduation such as publications, lectures and conference papers

Quality of the research project: originality, topicality and relevance, choice of host institution and first contacts, feasibility and consistency of study plan and schedule, and incorporation within the overall doctorate
Potential of the applicant: career prospects, motivation including German language skills if different from the working language, and non-study-related activities and civic engagement
coverage: Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Travel allowance, with an application required if the funding period exceeds six months
For a funding period of more than six months: research allowance of 460 euros, monthly rent subsidy and monthly allowance for accompanying members of family (on application after start of funding)

Only for a funding period of more than six months: course fees for an online language course, if necessary a German language course in Germany before the start of the research project, an allowance for a personally chosen German language course, and reimbursement of the fee for a TestDaF or DSH test
Green Mobility Top Up or reimbursement of carbon offset payments, plus on application an individual subsidy for justified additional costs in the case of a disability or chronic illness
application_method: Generate the recommendation form in the DAAD Portal under 'Create Letter of Recommendation Form' during the application period and send it to the university teacher
Complete the online application in full and upload all documents as PDF files in the 'Attachments' section
official.application_route: Register on the DAAD Portal and submit the online application with all PDF attachments during the annual application window, which opens at least six weeks before the deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants of any nationality doing their doctorate outside Germany; the application cannot be considered if the applicant has been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline.
official.international_eligibility: Open internationally; applicants doing their entire doctorate at a German university cannot apply, and eligibility is checked against the published country list on the announcement.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any subject area; for applicants from human medicine, veterinary medicine and dentistry, further subject-specific regulations apply.
official.research_requirement: A research project at a state or state-recognised university or a non-university research institute in Germany, agreed with a scientific supervisor in Germany; research work in countries other than Germany cannot be funded and the funding cannot be divided within the funding period.

official.description: The research grant offers the opportunity to realise a research project in Germany and supports research stays during a doctorate or in the early postdoc phase. The doctoral degree is awarded by the home university outside Germany, where the applicant is already registered.
official.program_type: Research stay grant for doctoral candidates and early postdocs
official.english_requirement: No English test score is required; the application and documents are handled in German or English, and documents in another national language need a German or English translation. Selection takes account of knowledge of the language of instruction or working language, and German skills are considered if different from the working language.

applicant_utility.summary: This grant funds a 2-12 month research stay in Germany for doctoral candidates registered outside Germany, or a 2-6 month stay for postdocs within four years of their doctorate, paying EUR 1,400 per month plus contributions to health, accident and liability insurance and a travel allowance. The extras that matter most unlock only if you stay longer than six months: a EUR 460 research allowance, rent subsidy, family allowance, German course support and TestDaF or DSH fee reimbursement. You must secure the German host and supervisor yourself before applying, the degree is still awarded by your home university, and the scholarship can neither be extended nor split.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Doctoral researchers in the first three years of a PhD done outside Germany, and recent postdocs, who can win a German host institute's backing for a defined project phase.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure the German supervisor first and obtain the host confirmation that references your project and guarantees a workplace, plus the supervisor's declaration on safety-relevant and ethical aspects
Draft the proposal within 10 pages and a 1-2 page motivation letter that tie the German phase explicitly into the overall doctorate
Ask your doctoral supervisor early for the recommendation letter on the DAAD form, which you generate inside the portal during the application window
Verify the 15-month rule: more than 15 months resident in Germany at the deadline ends your application
Assemble PDFs of every degree certificate and transcript, with German or English translations uploaded alongside the originals
common_rejection_risks: A German host invitation that is generic and does not guarantee a workplace or mention the actual project
A proposal that reads as a standalone trip rather than a phase embedded in the doctorate
Missing the most recent degree certificate without uploading a provisional document, or untranslated documents
A motivation letter that never answers what the applicant gains personally, professionally and career-wise from Germany
Uploading on the final day and losing the application to portal problems
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs above the 1,400-euro monthly rate, insurance costs beyond the DAAD contributions, and - for stays of six months or less - no rent subsidy at all. Large-city rental deposits, relocation costs, and family costs beyond the accompanying-member allowance are the applicant's own.
document_audit: Only PDFs upload, and DAAD can demand certified copies later, so keep scannable originals
Strict page limits: CV max 3 pages, publication list max 10 pages and mandatory for postdocs, proposal max 10 pages in total
The recommendation letter must be on the DAAD form generated in the portal, not a free-form referee letter
The supervisor's dual-use and ethics declaration is a separate document many applicants forget until the deadline
For doctoral candidates the proof of admission or enrolment must be uploaded under the correct portal slot
alerts: The 2027-start round is currently closed and new dates appear only in the second quarter of each year, so plan a full year ahead
The funding cannot be split or extended: the whole research phase must fit inside the funded months, and research outside Germany is ineligible
Third-party benefits are partially credited against the DAAD scholarship, so declare other funding
Residence over 15 months in Germany at the deadline is an automatic bar, even for earlier study stays
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the DAAD Portal, generate the recommendation form, complete the online form, upload every PDF, and submit well before the cutoff; portal access appears only during the application window.

official.application_cycle: Applications 1 September to 30 October each year; courses take place between June and September of the following year (2027 course cycle)
official.status_note: The announcement fixes the deadline as '30 October of each year, 23:59 (Central European Time)' with applications possible from 1 September each year; the current window runs 1 September to 30 October 2026 for courses in summer 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship covers the costs of the language course and provides single-room accommodation for the course duration; it is a short-course grant and publishes no degree tuition coverage.
benefits: Coverage of the costs for the language course
Provision of accommodation by the course provider for the duration of the course, in a single room such as a student dormitory, shared apartment or private household
Payment of a country-specific travel allowance
Health, accident and personal liability insurance benefits
eligibility: Applications are open to students and graduates in any subject area

Undergraduate students must have completed at least two academic years of university study by the time the funding period begins; final-year students are only eligible if they intend to undertake postgraduate studies immediately after graduating
The grant holder must be at least 18 years old when starting the language course

Applicants must be enrolled at a university in one of the programme-related countries (except Germany) both at the time of application and throughout the entire scholarship period; an application is not possible if enrolled at a German university at any time, for example in a double or joint degree programme
Applicants must be able to follow lectures in German and participate in group work; German language skills must be proven at the time of application
Funding from the programme can only be claimed once
requirements: Applications must be submitted online through the DAAD Portal between 1 September and 30 October; only PDF files can be uploaded

Applicants must name three courses at three different course locations; the DAAD reserves the right to assign a different course if capacities are limited, and course preferences cannot be changed once the application has been received
Participation is exclusively in person and the courses are taught exclusively in German; remote participation is not possible

German language proficiency must be proven with onSET-Deutsch, TestDaF, Goethe Institut Zertifikat, DSD, DSH, telc Deutsch or ÖSD-Zertifikat (for subject-specific language courses the Abitur is also accepted); the certificate cannot be older than one year at the time of application, or two years for B2 or TDN3 in all examination parts
The curriculum vitae and the letter of motivation must be written in German
Incomplete applications cannot be considered; the DAAD portal closes at 24:00 CET or CEST on the last application day
documents: Complete curriculum vitae in tabular form (in German) and letter of motivation (in German)

Transcripts of all university examinations taken in the last two consecutive years, including individual grades, in the original and with a German or English translation; if no two-year transcript exists because of a shorter period of study, proof of achievements for the current period plus the school-leaving certificate with individual grades
For graduates: the last university degree certificate with final grade, in the original and with a German or English translation
German language certificates, with a German or English translation where applicable

Other documents considered important, such as proof of internships or employment certificates, with translations where applicable; final-year undergraduates add a university certificate confirming the intention to undertake postgraduate study, or a clear statement of that intention
selection_criteria: Convincing letter of motivation for the choice of study programme and future academic project
coverage: Costs of the German language course
Accommodation in a single room provided by the course provider for the duration of the course, such as a student dormitory, shared apartment or private household
One-time allowance of 475 EUR, transferred by the DAAD to the course provider and disbursed in cash to scholarship holders on site
Country-specific travel allowance, likewise paid out in cash on site and not transferred abroad
Health, accident and personal liability insurance benefits
application_method: Register in the DAAD portal during the 1 September to 30 October application period
Complete the online application form, naming three courses at three different course locations
Upload all application documents as PDF files
official.application_route: Apply online via the DAAD Portal between 1 September and 30 October, naming three preferred courses at three different locations.
official.study_mode: Full-time course attendance (four weeks, max. 5 days per week, at least 25 teaching hours per week), in person only
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be enrolled at a university in one of the programme-related countries (except Germany) at the time of application and throughout the entire scholarship period; a German enrolment at any time rules the application out.
official.international_eligibility: Open to students and graduates in any subject area from the programme-related countries, enrolled outside Germany; at least 18 years old at the start of the course.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any subject area; undergraduate students must have completed at least two academic years of university study by the time the funding period begins.
official.duration: Four weeks (max. 5 days per week, at least 25 teaching hours per week); courses take place between June and September and the grants are not extendable
official.description: The aim of the programme is to deepen the knowledge of the German language, both in general language and technical language, and to augment the knowledge of the regional studies. Funding is provided for participation in language and cultural studies courses as well as technical language courses at German universities.
official.program_type: University Summer Courses (HSK) grant for four-week German language, cultural studies and technical language courses

applicant_utility.summary: This grant sends undergraduates and graduates to a four-week German language, cultural studies or technical language course at a German university, covering the course fee, a single room through the course provider, a EUR 475 one-off allowance, a country-specific travel allowance and insurance. The window is short and fixed: 1 September to 30 October each year at 23:59 CET, for courses running the following June to September. Because course capacity is limited you list three choices at three different locations and DAAD may place you elsewhere, and everything from the motivation letter to the classroom is in German, with a recognised certificate no older than one year.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students who have finished at least two years of university study, and graduates, enrolled outside Germany, who want an intensive four-week German-language summer at a German university.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your German certificate date now: onSET-Deutsch, TestDaF, Goethe, DSD, DSH, telc or ÖSD no older than one year, or B2/TDN3 in all parts within two years
Confirm you are, and will remain, enrolled outside Germany and never at a German university during the scholarship period
Write the CV and motivation letter in German, and gather two consecutive years of transcripts with translations
Shortlist three courses at three different locations from the official course list, since preferences lock on submission
Final-year students: obtain the university certificate confirming the plan to start postgraduate study
common_rejection_risks: An expired or unrecognised German language certificate, or a B2 certificate missing the two-year rule in all examination parts
Any German university enrolment, including a double or joint degree semester, at any point in the period
A motivation letter or CV not written in German
Transcripts that do not cover the last two consecutive years, or missing the school-leaving certificate when the programme is shorter
Assuming one of the three preferred courses is guaranteed despite limited capacity
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel costs beyond the country-specific travel allowance, personal spending beyond the EUR 475 cash allowance, and any extras such as course materials or leisure activities in the host city.
document_audit: Only PDFs upload, and translations must be uploaded together with the original-language document
Two consecutive years of transcripts are mandatory; shorter programmes additionally need the school-leaving certificate with individual grades
Graduates must include the latest degree certificate with the final grade, original plus translation
The EUR 475 allowance and travel allowance are paid in cash on site by the course provider, never into a foreign bank account, so plan the first days' expenses
The grant can only be claimed once in a lifetime, so choose the course year deliberately
alerts: The portal closes hard at 24:00 CET on 30 October and incomplete applications are not considered
Attendance is exclusively in person and exclusively in German; remote participation is impossible and the grant is not extendable
Course choice is final once submitted, and DAAD may reassign you to a different course or location
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the DAAD Portal, complete the online form naming three courses, upload the German-language documents as PDFs, and submit before 30 October 23:59 CET.
